blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 1.4
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 1.4

blocks.text: ज्ञानाधिष्ठानं मातृका
blocks.directed: [slowly] ज्ञानाधिष्ठानं मातृका

blocks.text: Jñānādhiṣṭhānaṃ mātṛkā.
blocks.directed: Jñānādhiṣṭhānaṃ mātṛkā.

blocks.text: Mātṛkā is the foundation of knowledge.
blocks.directed: Mātṛkā is the foundation of knowledge.

blocks.text: Your Alphabet Is Secretly Running the Show.
blocks.directed: Your Alphabet Is Secretly Running the Show.

blocks.text: Now things get properly tantric.
blocks.directed: Now things get properly tantric.

blocks.text: Mātṛkā means the little mother, or mother principle.
blocks.directed: Mātṛkā means the little mother, or mother principle.

blocks.text: Here she is the power associated with the Sanskrit phonemes — the letters from a through kṣa — as the basis of differentiated cognition.
blocks.directed: Here she is the power associated with the Sanskrit phonemes — the letters from a through kṣa — as the basis of differentiated cognition.

blocks.text: This isn’t just a bizarre claim that the alphabet invented your suffering.
blocks.directed: This isn’t just a bizarre claim that the alphabet invented your suffering.

blocks.text: The idea is much more sophisticated.
blocks.directed: The idea is much more sophisticated.

blocks.text: Language articulates experience.
blocks.directed: Language articulates experience.

blocks.text: Experience becomes conceptualised.
blocks.directed: Experience becomes conceptualised.

blocks.text: Conceptualisation helps establish distinctions.
blocks.directed: Conceptualisation helps establish distinctions.

blocks.text: Those distinctions become entangled with identity, memory, desire, aversion and the sense of being an individual subject surrounded by other things.
blocks.directed: Those distinctions become entangled with identity, memory, desire, aversion and the sense of being an individual subject surrounded by other things.

blocks.text: You perceive an event.
blocks.directed: You perceive an event.

blocks.text: Then language arrives.
blocks.directed: Then language arrives.

blocks.text: “This is terrible.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “This is terrible.”

blocks.text: “That person disrespected me.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “That person disrespected me.”

blocks.text: “I always fail.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I always fail.”

blocks.text: And an entire little world forms around the verbal construction.
blocks.directed: And an entire little world forms around the verbal construction.

blocks.text: You’ve transformed a passing occurrence into a personal cosmological crisis.
blocks.directed: You’ve transformed a passing occurrence into a personal cosmological crisis.

blocks.text: All before breakfast.
blocks.directed: All before breakfast.

blocks.text: For Kṣemarāja, however, Mātṛkā is not intrinsically evil.
blocks.directed: For Kṣemarāja, however, Mātṛkā is not intrinsically evil.

blocks.text: She is Śakti.
blocks.directed: She is Śakti.

blocks.text: The very same power that generates limitation can, when recognised, become a means of liberation.
blocks.directed: The very same power that generates limitation can, when recognised, become a means of liberation.

blocks.text: This is enormously important for understanding Trika’s fascination with Sanskrit phonemes, mantra, and the metaphysics of speech.
blocks.directed: This is enormously important for understanding Trika’s fascination with Sanskrit phonemes, mantra, and the metaphysics of speech.

blocks.text: Speech isn’t just a tool for describing an independently established universe.
blocks.directed: Speech isn’t just a tool for describing an independently established universe.

blocks.text: Within this tradition, it belongs to the very process by which consciousness manifests differentiated reality.
blocks.directed: Within this tradition, it belongs to the very process by which consciousness manifests differentiated reality.

blocks.text: The mother who makes the prison is also the mother who holds the key.
blocks.directed: The mother who makes the prison is also the mother who holds the key.

blocks.text: Rather inconvenient for the prison authorities, who are also Śiva.
blocks.directed: Rather inconvenient for the prison authorities, who are also Śiva.
